mainTopic: Women's obligations in time-bound מצוות, קידוש and ברכת המזון, and the rules for a בעל קרי
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה: נשים are exempt from קריאת שמע and תפילין, but obligated in תפילה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון. For each item the גמרא asks 'isn't that obvious?' and answers with a מהו דתימא, a reason we might have ruled the other way. רב אדא בר אהבה then rules that women are obligated in קידוש by Torah law. אביי calls it only rabbinic, but רבא rejects that and proves it from זכור and שמור. רבינא asks whether women's ברכת המזון is Torah or rabbinic, which decides whether a woman can say it for her husband. A ברייתא is brought as proof, but it is pushed off as dealing with someone who ate only a rabbinic amount. That leads to an אגדה: הקב״ה favors ישראל because they bless even after a כזית or כביצה. Then a new משנה rules on a בעל קרי, and רבינא and רב חסדא disagree whether thinking the words counts like saying them.

steps.title: End of the משנה: exempt from תפילין, obligated in תפילה, מזוזה and ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list. נשים are exempt from תפילין, but they are obligated in תפילה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And women are exempt from תפילין, but they are obligated in prayer, מזוזה, and Grace after Meals.
steps.whatsHappening: We are reading the end of a משנה that started on the previous page. It finishes listing what נשים are exempt from, and then lists what they are obligated in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two lists. The exempt list is קריאת שמע and תפילין. The obligated list is תפילה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון. The גמרא will now explain why each item had to be mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Tefillin, the leather boxes with פסוקים worn on the arm and head
Prayer (the עמידה / שמונה עשרה)
The parchment with פסוקים fixed on the doorpost
The blessings said after eating a bread meal
They are obligated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up תְּפִלִּין (the boxes worn on the arm and head, which נשים are exempt from) with תְּפִלָּה (prayer, which they are obligated in). The words look almost the same.

phrases.english: And from tefillin,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: נשים, slaves, and children are exempt from קריאת שמע and from תפילין.

phrases.english: but they are obligated in prayer and in mezuzah
and in Grace after Meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה that began on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נשים are exempt from קריאת שמע and תפילין, but obligated in תפילה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Why mention שמע? Isn't it obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say נשים are exempt from קריאת שמע. It is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and נשים are exempt from all of those.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמע — that is obvious! It is a time-bound positive מצוה, and from every time-bound positive מצוה women are exempt. So why say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a challenge. Why did the משנה bother to say something we already know from a general rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע is only said at set times, morning and night. That makes it a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. Since there is already a general rule that נשים are exempt from such מצוות, listing קריאת שמע seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
It's obvious! (a challenge: why did this need to be said?)
A positive מצוה that only applies at certain times
Exempt (said about women)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that נשים are exempt from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא is the background for this whole section.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The recitation of Shema: that is obvious!
It is a positive מצוה that is caused by time,
and from every time-bound positive מצוה
women are exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משנה to list קריאת שמע
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of קריאת שמע as an exemption for נשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general rule already exempts נשים from every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so stating this case adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought accepting God's kingship obligates women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought נשים are obligated, because קריאת שמע contains קבלת עול מלכות שמים. The משנה teaches that they are still exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since שמע contains the acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven, women should be obligated. So the משנה teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It names a reason we might have made an exception for קריאת שמע, and says the משנה is telling us not to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע is special because it expresses accepting God as King. That could have made it important enough to obligate everyone, even though it is time-bound. The משנה teaches that the general rule still applies, and נשים are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: What might you have said? (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Since, because
The kingship of Heaven, accepting God as King
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: The reason after מהו דתימא is what we would have WRONGLY thought. The final halacha is the opposite: נשים are exempt from קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
Since it contains the kingdom of Heaven, [women should be obligated],
it teaches us [that they are exempt].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge about קריאת שמע
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the case is not obvious, because there was a reason to think otherwise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because קריאת שמע contains מלכות שמים, נשים might be obligated even though it is time-bound.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with מלכות שמים, נשים are exempt from קריאת שמע under the general time-bound rule.

steps.title: Why mention תפילין? Isn't that obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about תפילין. It is also time-bound, so why did the משנה need to list it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And from תפילין — that is obvious too! Why did the משנה need to say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה and asks the same 'isn't it obvious?' question. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא treats תפילין as another מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so the general rule should already exempt נשים. The question has the same shape as the one about קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from tefillin', the words of the משנה being discussed

phrases.english: And from tefillin. That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same פשיטא challenge, now about תפילין
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of תפילין as an exemption for נשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and the general rule already exempts נשים.

steps.title: We might have compared תפילין to מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah places תפילין next to מזוזה, and נשים are obligated in מזוזה. So we might have thought they are obligated in תפילין too. The משנה teaches that they are still exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since תפילין is compared to מזוזה, women should be obligated in תפילין just as they are in מזוזה. So the משנה teaches us that they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to mention תפילין. A comparison to מזוזה could have misled us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים about תפילין and מזוזה come right next to each other, which creates a הקש, a link between the two מצוות. Since נשים are obligated in מזוזה, we might have applied that to תפילין as well. The משנה teaches that the time-bound rule wins, and נשים are exempt from תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: It is compared (linked by placement in the Torah)
A comparison drawn from two topics placed side by side in the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Both answers use the same pattern. A special reason (מלכות שמים, or the הקש to מזוזה) might have obligated נשים, but the משנה teaches that the time-bound rule still exempts them from קריאת שמע and תפילין.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
Since it is compared to mezuzah, [women should be obligated, as they are in mezuzah] —
phrases.notes: The פסוקים sit right next to each other: תפילין in דברים 6:8, מזוזה in דברים 6:9.

phrases.english: it teaches us [that they are exempt].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge about תפילין
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the case is not obvious, because a הקש could have pointed the other way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because תפילין is linked by הקש to מזוזה, in which נשים are obligated, נשים might be obligated in תפילין too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Despite the הקש, נשים are exempt from תפילין because it is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא.

steps.title: Women are obligated in prayer because it is a request for mercy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why נשים are obligated in תפילה even though it is said at set times: תפילה is asking for mercy, and everyone needs mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they are obligated in prayer.' Why? Because prayer is asking for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, תפילה, and gives the reason women are obligated: prayer is a request for רחמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a hidden question here. תפילה is said at fixed times, so it looks like a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, which women are usually exempt from. The answer is that תפילה is basically asking ה׳ for mercy, and women need mercy just like men.

keyTerms.meaning: Prayer (שמונה עשרה)
Mercy; a request for compassion
They are; it is

phrases.english: And they are obligated in prayer.
Because it is a request for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exemptions (קריאת שמע, תפילין) to the obligations in the משנה, starting with תפילה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason for the obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תפילה is said at fixed times, so women should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: תפילה is a request for mercy, which applies to everyone.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to say women must pray
steps.stepSummary: Since a פסוק mentions praying evening, morning, and noon, we might have thought תפילה is time-bound and women are exempt. The משנה teaches that they are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written about prayer 'Evening, morning, and noon,' it is like a time-bound מצוה. So the משנה teaches us that women are still obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to say this at all: there was a reason to think women might be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תפילה is asking for mercy, the obligation seems obvious. But a פסוק ties prayer to three times of day, which could make it look like a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. The משנה tells us not to think that way.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said / you might have thought
It teaches us (that this is not so)
Since; because
Is similar to; is considered like

phrases.english: You might have said:
Since it is written about it
'Evening and morning and noon,'
it is like a time-bound positive מצוה
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה needed to state the obligation from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the possible mistake the משנה prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a פסוק ties prayer to set times, it is time-bound and women are exempt.

steps.title: Isn't the מזוזה obligation obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next item, מזוזה, and asks why it needed saying. מזוזה is not time-bound, so women should obviously be obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in מזוזה.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: why would it need to tell us something so obvious? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are only exempt from time-bound positive מצוות‎. מזוזה applies all the time, so there seems to be no reason to exempt them. The משנה's statement looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (Why say it?)
The scroll fixed on the doorpost

phrases.english: And in mezuzah.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next obligation listed in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that women are obligated in מזוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מזוזה is not time-bound, so the obligation is obvious and the statement seems extra.

steps.title: מזוזה is placed next to Torah study
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought women are exempt from מזוזה because the Torah places it next to תלמוד תורה, which women are exempt from. The משנה teaches they are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since מזוזה is compared to Torah study, women are exempt. So the משנה teaches us that they are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8 by showing a real reason someone might have exempted women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah, the פסוק about learning Torah sits right next to the פסוק about מזוזה. Women are exempt from תלמוד תורה, so one might compare the two and exempt them from מזוזה too. The משנה rules out that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared (placed side by side in the Torah)
The מצוה of learning Torah

steps.confusionAlert: In Step 5, the closeness of תפילין to מזוזה almost made women obligated in תפילין. Here, the closeness of מזוזה to תלמוד תורה almost made them exempt from מזוזה. Each time the משנה rejects the comparison.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since it is compared to Torah study,
phrases.notes: In דברים 11:19–20, learning Torah and מזוזה come one right after the other.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that women are obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִתַּקַּשׁ לְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא based on a comparison (הקש) in the Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מזוזה is compared to תלמוד תורה, so women are exempt.

steps.title: Isn't the Grace after Meals obligation obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next item, ברכת המזון, and asks why it needed saying, since it seems clearly not time-bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in Grace after Meals.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same 'that's obvious' question about ברכת המזון. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת המזון depends on eating, not on a time of day. So women should obviously be obligated, and the משנה's statement looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Grace after Meals; the blessing after eating bread

phrases.english: And in Grace after Meals.
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as Step 8, now on the last item in the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that women are obligated in ברכת המזון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ברכת המזון is not time-bound, so the obligation is obvious.

steps.title: A verse links meals to evening and morning
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק speaks of meat in the evening and bread in the morning, so we might have thought ברכת המזון is time-bound. The משנה teaches women are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written 'When ה׳ gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to be full,' it is like a time-bound מצוה. So the משנה teaches us that women are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 10 by pointing to a פסוק that could make ברכת המזון look time-bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties eating to evening and morning. One might think meals, and so ברכת המזון, have fixed times, making it a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. The משנה teaches it is not, so women are obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: When (ה׳) gives
To be satisfied; to be full

steps.whatToRemember: For each obligation in the משנה (תפילה, מזוזה, ברכת המזון), the גמרא finds a reason we might have wrongly exempted women, and the משנה tells us they are obligated.

phrases.english: You might have said:
since it is written
'When ה׳ gives you in the evening
meat to eat
and bread in the morning to be full,'
it is like a time-bound positive מצוה
so it teaches us that it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meals have set times, so ברכת המזון is time-bound and women are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are obligated in ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Women are obligated in קידוש by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה rules that נשים are obligated in קידוש היום on שבת מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Women are obligated in sanctifying the day (קידוש) by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins: רב אדא בר אהבה rules that women must say קידוש on שבת, and that this is a Torah obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not part of the משנה's list. The surprising part is 'by Torah law', since קידוש happens on a set day.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctifying the day; Kiddush on שבת
By Torah law (דאורייתא)

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Women are obligated in sanctifying the day
by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about another מצוה that women are obligated in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in קידוש on שבת מדאורייתא.

steps.title: But קידוש is a time-bound מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה: קידוש is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are exempt from all of those.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? It is a time-bound positive מצוה, and women are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling using the general rule about time-bound מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש is only said on שבת, a set time. By the general rule, women should be exempt. So how can רב אדא בר אהבה say they are obligated by Torah law?

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Exempt (said of women)

phrases.english: Why?
It is a time-bound positive מצוה,
and from every time-bound positive מצוה
women are exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that the obligation is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule exempts women from time-bound positive מצוות, and קידוש is one of them.

steps.title: אביי: the obligation is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that women are obligated in קידוש only מדרבנן, not by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a rabbinic obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by changing the level of the obligation: women must make קידוש, but only because the רבנן required it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי keeps the general rule in place. Since קידוש is time-bound, women are exempt by Torah law, and their obligation comes only from the רבנן. This goes against רב אדא בר אהבה's words 'by Torah law', and רבא points that out in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Lowers the obligation from Torah level to rabbinic level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women are obligated in קידוש by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are obligated in קידוש only מדרבנן.

steps.title: רבא rejects אביי's rabbinic-only answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives two objections to אביי. First, רב אדא בר אהבה clearly said women's קידוש is דבר תורה. Second, if the Rabbis obligated women here, why not obligate them in every time-bound מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But רב אדא בר אהבה said 'by Torah law'! And furthermore, if so, let us obligate women in all positive מצוות by rabbinic law!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer from Step 14 with two separate problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Problem one: אביי's answer goes against the wording of רב אדא בר אהבה, who said women's קידוש is מדאורייתא, not מדרבנן. Problem two: אביי gives no reason why קידוש is special. If the Rabbis can obligate women without a reason, they could do it for every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and they clearly did not.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law; the same as מִדְּאוֹרַיְיתָא
And furthermore; it introduces a second objection
By rabbinic law
Let us obligate them

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But he said "by Torah law"!
phrases.notes: "He" is רב אדא בר אהבה, whose ruling started this discussion.

phrases.english: And furthermore, all positive מצוות
let us obligate them [women] by rabbinic law!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא ״דְּבַר תּוֹרָה״ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that women are obligated in קידוש only מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer goes against רב אדא בר אהבה's explicit words 'דבר תורה'. It also gives no reason to single out קידוש, so it would require a rabbinic obligation in every time-bound מצוה.

steps.title: רבא's Torah source: Remember and Observe
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the two wordings of the Ten Commandments, זכור and שמור, that whoever must keep שבת's prohibitions must also do קידוש. Women must keep the prohibitions, so they are obligated in קידוש מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The verse says 'Remember' and 'Observe'. Anyone who is included in observing is included in remembering. Since women are included in observing, they are included in remembering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer. He defends רב אדא בר אהבה with a Torah source that makes קידוש an exception for women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמור means not breaking שבת's prohibitions, and women are fully obligated in those. זכור means actively remembering שבת through קידוש. Because the Torah links the two words, the active מצוה follows the prohibitions, so women are obligated even though קידוש is time-bound.

keyTerms.meaning: Remember; the positive מצוה of שבת, done through קִידּוּשׁ
Observe; keeping שבת's prohibitions
Since

steps.whatToRemember: Women are obligated in קידוש מדאורייתא, because זכור and שמור are linked. Whoever must keep שבת's prohibitions must also say קידוש.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean קידוש stops being a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. It is still time-bound. The זכור/שמור link is a special exception that obligates women anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical halacha that women are obligated in קידוש on שבת by Torah law.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse says "Remember" and "Observe":
phrases.notes: שמות 20:8 says זכור, and דברים 5:12 says שמור.

phrases.english: anyone who is included in observing
is included in remembering.
And these women, since they are included in observing,
are included in remembering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״זָכוֹר וְשָׁמוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected אביי's answer, רבא answers the question from Step 13 in a new way.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A Torah verse creates a special exception to the time-bound exemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since קידוש is time-bound, women should be exempt, or at most obligated מדרבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The link between זכור and שמור obligates women in קידוש מדאורייתא, even though it is time-bound.

steps.title: Is women's Grace after Meals Torah or rabbinic?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא whether women's obligation in ברכת המזון is דאורייתא or דרבנן. The practical difference is whether a woman can say it on behalf of men who are obligated by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: Are women obligated in Grace after Meals by Torah law or rabbinic law? What difference does it make? Whether they can fulfill the obligation of others. If it is Torah law, one obligated by Torah law can fulfill the obligation of others obligated by Torah law. But if it is rabbinic, she counts as 'one who is not obligated in the matter', and such a person cannot fulfill the obligation of others. So what is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks a new question about the משנה's ruling that women are obligated in ברכת המזון. He also explains why the answer matters in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said women are obligated, but it did not say at what level. A person can only fulfill someone else's obligation if his own obligation is at least as strong. So if a woman's obligation is only דרבנן, she could not cover a man who is obligated מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
To fulfill their obligation for them, by saying it on their behalf
One who is not obligated in the matter
Granted; this works out fine
What? It asks for the answer

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Women in Grace after Meals,
is it by Torah law or by rabbinic law?
What difference does it make?
To fulfill the obligation of others.
Granted, if you say it is Torah law,
one obligated by Torah law comes and fulfills the obligation of one obligated by Torah law.
But if you say it is rabbinic,
she is "one who is not obligated in the matter,"
and anyone who is not obligated in the matter

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: cannot fulfill the obligation of the many.
What is the answer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: נָשִׁים בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן, דְאוֹרָיְיתָא אוֹ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from קידוש back to the משנה's ruling on ברכת המזון, and asks how strong the obligation is.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether women's obligation in ברכת המזון is דאורייתא or דרבנן. This decides whether a woman can say it on behalf of men obligated by Torah law.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a wife may bless for her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer רבינא's question with a ברייתא. A son may say the blessing for his father, a slave for his master, and a wife for her husband, though the Sages cursed a man who needs this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: In truth they said that a son may bless on behalf of his father, a slave on behalf of his master, and a woman on behalf of her husband. But the Sages said: May a curse come upon a man whose wife and children bless for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא as a first attempt to answer רבינא's question. This sets up the discussion that follows about what it really proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a wife may say ברכת המזון for her husband, so she can fulfill his obligation. That seems to show her obligation is as strong as his, דאורייתא. The ברייתא also adds that it is shameful for a man to need someone else to bless for him.

keyTerms.meaning: In truth they said; it introduces an accepted ruling
Says the blessing on behalf of someone
A curse

steps.confusionAlert: The curse does not cancel the ruling. The blessing still works, and a wife does fulfill her husband's obligation. The curse only criticizes a man who cannot say ברכת המזון himself.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In truth they said
a son may bless on behalf of his father
and a slave may bless on behalf of his master
and a woman may bless on behalf of her husband,
but the Sages said:
May a curse come upon a man
whose wife and children bless for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ בֵּן מְבָרֵךְ לְאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to answer רבינא's question from Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That women's obligation in ברכת המזון is דאורייתא, since a wife can fulfill her husband's obligation
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a son, a slave and a wife may each say ברכת המזון on behalf of the father, master or husband

steps.title: The proof: only a Torah-level obligation can cover a Torah-level obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא. A wife may bless for her husband, so her obligation must be דאורייתא like his.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if her obligation is from the Torah, because a Torah-obligated person can fulfill the duty of another Torah-obligated person. But if her obligation is only rabbinic, how could she fulfill the duty of someone obligated by the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started with the ברייתא. Since a wife may say ברכת המזון for her husband, her obligation must be from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule behind the proof is that someone can only fulfill an obligation for another person if his own obligation is at least as strong. A rabbinic obligation cannot cover a Torah obligation. So if a wife can cover her husband, she must be obligated מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say... (sets up one side that works and one that does not)
From the Torah, by Torah law
From the Rabbis, by rabbinic law
Takes out, meaning he fulfills someone else's obligation for him

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the basic rule of fulfilling an obligation for others: the one saying the ברכה must be obligated at the same level or higher.

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say it is by Torah law,
one obligated by Torah law comes and exempts one obligated by Torah law.
But if you say it is by rabbinic law,
can one obligated by rabbinic law come and exempt one obligated by Torah law?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun with the ברייתא in Step 18 by spelling out what it shows.
steps.raayaObject: That women are obligated in ברכת המזון מדאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a wife may say ברכת המזון for her husband, combined with the rule that a rabbinic obligation cannot cover a Torah obligation

steps.title: But a minor is also listed, and he is not obligated at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The same ברייתא lets a son bless for his father, and a minor has no Torah obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, is a minor obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. If the ברייתא only allows people with a Torah obligation, how can it include a son who may be a minor?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is not obligated in מצוות by Torah law, yet the ברייתא says a son may bless for his father. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about a father with a Torah-level obligation. That means it proves nothing about women.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the other side's logic against them)
A minor, a child under the age of מצוות
Someone who is obligated

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
is a minor someone who is obligated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from Step 19 by pointing to another person in the same ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא, not the possibility that women are obligated מדאורייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא includes a minor, who has no Torah obligation, so it cannot be about a Torah-level obligation

steps.title: The ברייתא is about someone who ate only a rabbinic amount
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is re-explained: the father ate less than a filling meal, so his own obligation is only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? Where he ate only the amount the Rabbis require a blessing for. Then one with a rabbinic obligation comes and fulfills it for one with a rabbinic obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to read the ברייתא. The father ate only a small amount, so he needs ברכת המזון only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, ברכת המזון is required only after eating until full. If the father ate less, his obligation is rabbinic, so a son, slave, or wife with a rabbinic obligation can cover him. The ברייתא therefore does not answer רבינא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower reading)
An amount that only the Rabbis require a ברכה for

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא decided that women are obligated only מדרבנן. It only showed that this ברייתא does not prove either side, so רבינא's question stays open.

phrases.english: Rather, what are we dealing with here?
A case where he ate an amount that is only rabbinic,
phrases.notes: He ate enough to need a ברכה, but not enough to be full.

phrases.english: so one obligated by rabbinic law comes and exempts one obligated by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא can include a minor, which removes it as a proof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about a father with a full Torah obligation, so anyone covering him must also be Torah-obligated
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a father who ate only a rabbinic amount, so rabbinic-level people can cover him. Nothing is proven about women.

steps.title: The angels ask why הקב״ה shows favor to ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא teaches an אגדה: the angels point out that the Torah says הקב״ה shows no favor, yet ברכת כהנים says He does favor ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רבי אמי and sometimes in the name of רבי אסי: The ministering angels said to הקב״ה, 'Master of the world, Your Torah says You do not show favor or take bribes. Yet You show favor to ישראל, as it says, May ה׳ lift His face toward you!'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just mentioned the rabbinic amount for ברכת המזון, it brings a related אגדה. The angels point out what looks like a contradiction between two פסוקים, and the next step gives הקב״ה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One פסוק says הקב״ה does not show favor. Another פסוק, from ברכת כהנים, says He does favor ישראל. The angels' question sets up the answer, which ties back to ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded, taught a lesson from the פסוקים
The ministering angels
Shows favor, literally 'lifts the face'
A bribe

phrases.english: Rav Avira expounded,

phrases.aramaic: זִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Ami

phrases.aramaic: וְזִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Asi:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe, it is written in Your Torah:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים וְלֹא יִקַּח שֹׁחַד״,
phrases.english: 'Who does not show favor and does not take a bribe,'
yet You show favor to Israel,
as it is written: 'May ה׳ lift His face toward you'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the idea of a rabbinic amount for ברכת המזון from Step 21 and opens an אגדה about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: How הקב״ה can favor ישראל when the Torah says He shows no favor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two פסוקים seem to contradict: one says He shows no favor, the other says He favors ישראל.

steps.title: ישראל earn favor by blessing even after a small amount
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה answers: the Torah requires a ברכה only after eating until full, but ישראל bless even after a כזית or כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Should I not show favor to ישראל? I wrote in the Torah, You shall eat and be satisfied, and bless ה׳ your God. Yet they are strict with themselves and bless even after an olive's size or an egg's size.'
steps.whatsHappening: הקב״ה answers the angels. ישראל go beyond what the Torah asks, so He goes beyond strict judgment for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the ברכה to being full, so by Torah law a small snack needs no ברכת המזון. ישראל took on a ברכה even for a כזית or כביצה, which is the rabbinic amount from Step 21. Since they are extra careful with Him, He shows them extra favor.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall eat, be full, and bless, the Torah source for ברכת המזון
Are exacting, strict
An olive's size, a small amount of food
An egg's size

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, ברכת המזון is required only after eating until full. The obligation after a כזית or כביצה is a stricter practice that ישראל took on, and the אגדה says this is why הקב״ה favors them.

phrases.english: He said to them:
And should I not show favor to Israel,
for I wrote for them in the Torah:
'And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless ה׳ your God,'
phrases.notes: דברים 8:10. The point is the word 'satisfied': the Torah asks for the ברכה once you are full.

phrases.english: and they are strict with themselves
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: even for an olive's size and even for an egg's size.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם וְכִי לֹא אֶשָּׂא פָּנִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the angels' question from Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the favor as a fair response to ישראל's extra devotion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Favoring ישראל goes against the Torah's statement that הקב״ה shows no favor
steps.terutzMaskana: ישראל go beyond the letter of the law by blessing after small amounts, so they deserve favor in return

steps.title: New משנה: what a בעל קרי may say in שמע and ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: A בעל קרי thinks שמע in his mind without its ברכות. For food he blesses after but not before. רבי יהודה says he blesses before and after in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A בעל קרי thinks the שמע in his heart, and does not say the ברכות before it or after it. For food, he says the ברכה afterward but not the one before. רבי יהודה says: he says the ברכות before and after both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on what a person who is a בעל קרי may say aloud, and רבי יהודה disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל קרי was limited in saying words of Torah until he immersed, so the תנא keeps him to the minimum. He only thinks שמע, and for food he says only the ברכה after eating, which is from the Torah, not the one before, which is rabbinic. רבי יהודה is lenient and lets him say all the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה
A man who became impure from a seminal emission
Thinks the words in his heart without saying them aloud
Over food, meaning the ברכות on eating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two pairs of 'before and after.' For שמע, he says neither ברכה. For food, he says only the ברכה after eating.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who had a seminal emission thinks it in his heart,
phrases.notes: The משנה is still talking about קריאת שמע. He thinks the words without saying them.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, לֹא לְפָנֶיהָ וְלֹא לְאַחֲרֶיהָ.
phrases.english: and does not say a blessing, neither before it nor after it.
And over food he blesses afterward
but does not bless beforehand.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He blesses before them and after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and topic after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי thinks שמע without its ברכות and says only the ברכה after food. רבי יהודה lets him say the ברכות before and after both.

steps.title: רבינא: thinking counts like speaking
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns from the משנה that הרהור (thinking the words) counts like דבור (saying them). Otherwise, why would the משנה tell a בעל קרי to think שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבינא said: This teaches that thinking counts like speaking. For if you thought it did not count like speaking, why would he think the words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא on the משנה opens. רבינא draws a rule from the case of the בעל קרי who thinks שמע in his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 24) told the בעל קרי to think שמע in his mind. רבינא argues that this instruction only makes sense if thinking actually achieves something. So he concludes that thinking the words counts like saying them.

keyTerms.meaning: "This teaches": a rule is being drawn from the source just quoted
Thinking the words in one's mind without saying them
Counts like speech
"For if you would think…": introduces the opposite idea in order to reject it

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ravina said:
This teaches
that thinking counts like speaking.
For if you would think
that it does not count like speaking,
why would he think the words?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the משנה's ruling in step 24 that a בעל קרי thinks שמע in his mind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הרהור כדבור דמי: thinking the words counts like saying them.

steps.title: If thinking counts, why not say it aloud?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא: if thinking is the same as speaking, the בעל קרי should just say the words with his lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that thinking counts like speaking? Then let him say it with his lips!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבינא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If thinking and speaking are equal, then permitting one should mean permitting the other. So why does the משנה allow thinking but not saying the words aloud? It seems the משנה treats the two differently.

keyTerms.meaning: "But what then?": opens a challenge to the previous claim
Let him say it with his lips, aloud

phrases.english: But what are you saying?
That thinking counts like speaking?
Then let him say it with his lips!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, יוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבינא's inference from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that הרהור כדבור דמי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are truly equal, the משנה's distinction (thinking allowed, speaking not) makes no sense.

steps.title: Just as we found at Mount סיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that saying the words aloud is held back because of what happened at סיני, where people had to be pure before the Torah was spoken.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we found at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבינא with a short answer pointing to Mount סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At סיני, men who had been with their wives had to immerse before receiving the Torah, which was given through speech. Following that model, a בעל קרי may not say Torah words aloud until he immerses. Thinking can still count as speech for the obligation, while saying the words aloud has this extra restriction.

keyTerms.meaning: "As we found": pointing to a known precedent
Mount Sinai, where the Torah was given
Immersion in a מקוה to become pure

phrases.english: As we found at Sinai.
phrases.notes: Before the Torah was given, the men were told to keep away from their wives (שמות 19:15), so it was spoken aloud only to people who were pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 26 and keeps רבינא's rule standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a separate source for the restriction on speaking aloud, so the restriction does not prove that thinking is unlike speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's ban on saying the words aloud shows that thinking is weaker than speaking.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban on speaking aloud comes from the precedent of סיני. Thinking can still count like speech.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say thinking is weaker than speaking. It says speaking aloud has a special restriction for a בעל קרי, based on סיני.

steps.title: רב חסדא: thinking does not count like speaking
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns the opposite from the same משנה: thinking is not like speaking. If it were, the בעל קרי should just say the words aloud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Thinking does not count like speaking. For if you thought that thinking counts like speaking, let him say it with his lips.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב חסדא, reads the same משנה and draws the opposite rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא uses the same reasoning as the earlier challenge. The משנה allows thinking but does not allow speaking. So, in his view, the two must not be equal, and the thinking does not count as saying the words.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not count like speech

steps.whatToRemember: רבינא says הרהור כדבור דמי (thinking counts like speech). The Sinai precedent explains why a בעל קרי still may not speak aloud. רב חסדא says thinking does not count like speech, since otherwise he should just say the words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This disagreement affects whether a person who only thinks שמע or other required words has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Thinking does not count like speaking.
For if you would think
that thinking counts like speaking,
then let him say it with his lips.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר, הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite reading of the same משנה, using the logic of the challenge in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הרהור לאו כדבור דמי: thinking the words does not count like saying them.

steps.title: If thinking does not count, why think at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: if הרהור is not like דבור, the משנה's instruction to think שמע seems pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that thinking is not like speaking? If so, why does he think the words at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא from Step 28. If thinking the words does nothing, why does the משנה tell the בעל קרי to think them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said thinking is not the same as speaking, so the בעל קרי does not fulfill the מצוה by thinking. That leaves a gap: the משנה still tells him to think שמע. The גמרא wants to know what purpose that serves.

keyTerms.meaning: But what, then? This opens a challenge to the view just stated.
Not
Is similar to, is considered like
Why

phrases.english: But what, then? Thinking
is not like speaking?
Why does he think the words?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's reading in Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's view that הרהור is not like דבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If thinking accomplishes nothing, the משנה's instruction to think שמע has no purpose.

steps.title: So he will not sit idle while everyone else is busy
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the בעל קרי thinks שמע so he will not sit doing nothing while everyone around him says שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The purpose is that it should not happen that everyone is busy with שמע while he sits there idle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question from Step 29. The thinking is not meant to fulfill the מצוה. It keeps the בעל קרי involved instead of sitting idle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer lets רב חסדא's view stand. Thinking the words does not fulfill the obligation. It has a separate purpose: it keeps the person from looking and acting cut off while the community says שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: In order that it should not happen
Are busy with, engaged in
Sits idle, doing nothing

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
So that it should not be that everyone
is busy with it
phrases.notes: "It" means קריאת שמע, which everyone else is saying.

phrases.english: while he sits idle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כׇּל הָעוֹלָם עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different purpose for the instruction (not fulfilling the מצוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Thinking שמע only makes sense if it fulfills the obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thinking שמע keeps the בעל קרי from sitting idle while the community is engaged.

steps.title: Then let him learn a different section
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the goal is only to avoid sitting idle, he could learn any other part of Torah instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him study a different section!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's answer. If the only goal is to keep busy, why does it have to be שמע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's reason is about keeping busy. But any Torah learning would keep him busy. So the reason does not explain why the משנה chose שמע in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him study, recite
A different section or chapter

phrases.english: Let him study a different section!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's answer in Step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reason that thinking שמע is only to avoid sitting idle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any other learning would keep him busy, so the reason does not explain why it must be שמע.

steps.title: He should be busy with what the community is busy with
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that it is fitting to be engaged in the same thing the ציבור is doing, so he thinks שמע specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: He should be busy with the same thing the community is busy with.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers Step 31. The goal is to keep busy and also to join what the ציבור is doing, and right now they are saying שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer adds to רבי אלעזר's reason. It is not enough to keep busy with something. The person should connect to the community's activity, so only thinking שמע works.

keyTerms.meaning: The community, the congregation
With a matter, with a thing

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, thinking שמע does not fulfill the מצוה. The בעל קרי thinks it so he will not sit idle (רבי אלעזר), and specifically שמע so he joins what the ציבור is doing (רב אדא בר אהבה).

phrases.english: רב אדא בר אהבה said:
With a matter that the community is busy with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 31 and completes רבי אלעזר's explanation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Makes the reason more specific: the point is joining the community's activity, not just keeping busy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any learning would do, since the only goal is not to sit idle.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must be engaged in the same thing as the ציבור, which is שמע.
